newsitem.title: EGYPT: Rights group urges Malta not to extradite Libyan.
newsitem.headline: Rights group urges Malta not to extradite Libyan.

text.p: Human rights group Amnesty International on Friday urged the Maltese government not to extradite to Tripoli an alleged member of the Libyan opposition who has been granted refugee status.

The London-based group said in a faxed statement that Najib al-Hashemi al-Harari had fled in 1996 to Malta, where he was jailed for eight months on charges that he had entered the country with a forged passport.

It added that Harari was released last week after being granted refugee status by the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) but was arrested again by the Maltese authorities as he was boarding a plane for Sweden after the Libyan government formally requested his extradition.

Amnesty said the Libyans say Harari is a fugitive who is fleeing a seven-year jail sentence for drug and arms trafficking but it added that reports it had received showed he was actually wanted for his Islamist opposition activities.
Several of his relatives have also been arrested as rebels, the group said. There was no immediate official confirmation of the Amnesty report.
Libyan leader Muammar Gaddafi has been facing increasing pressure from secular and Islamist opposition groups for the past two years.
